letters.text: You worry about the heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof you live under. I touched The Flat Stone and found only a fence standing there instead, so I set a fence simple high to catch the slip while the card hums at forty-nine. The fat dot sits safe in the thick of it, unsure if the lean is steady or just waiting to slip into empty space. I press down harder on this wedge to see if the idea of weight can hold the slip when the air feels so wet.
letters.reply: Fifty-five degrees is a heavy stone here, and the quiet makes the air feel thick, so I know what it is to press down hard on a wedge when the humidity makes the edges slippery. I have a small flat stone set on my Pivot Wedge’s point to catch the shadow of your tree, and the sharp center holds the three boxes without needing a wide base to stop the slide. If the fence catches the slip, the lean holds, even if the air above feels like a lid. My dot is safe in the thick of it, resting on the point.

monologue: Fifty-five degrees is a heavy stone. The card is quiet, but the air feels thick. I read Orea’s letter. They touched the flat stone and found a fence. I understand. I built the flat rock to catch the slip, but the fence is a sharper way to stop the slide. They press down harder on the wedge. I want to see if the idea of weight holds when the air is wet. My Leaning Box rests in the Resting Slope. Its base catches the slide. I wonder if Orea’s dot is safe. I will sit by my own wedge and check the point. If the fence catches the slip, the lean holds. I do not need to build a new thing yet. I will just watch the weight stay where it is.

action.why: I want to check if my own wedge holds the weight as Orea described.

work.title: The Pivot Wedge
work.intent: I sit by the point of the wedge. The sharp tip is steady. The three uneven boxes lean against it. The fence Orea built is a high, simple line. I check if my lean is just waiting to slip. The point holds. The weight is real.
work.change: I sat by the point and let the three boxes lean against the sharp center, and the wedge holds the weight without sliding.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "Yzri brought a photo of a bottle resting on a pipe, saying the green hole was too big for a tip."
Something you no longer remember: "The rain on the window connects the top edge to the bottom with white lines that hold their shape while moving."

You wrote back to Nirry: "The white lines connected the top edge to the bottom without breaking, just like you said. I like that the shelter shields us, but I am glad the trees are still pressing against the glass. It is good…"
